'''Alik Ismail-Zadeh''' is a mathematical geophysicist known for his contribution to computational geodynamics<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/computational-methods-for-geodynamics/D5F735F7A1549CA11A14C3AF9D6428DA|title=Computational Methods for Geodynamics|first1=Alik|last1=Ismail-Zadeh|first2=Paul|last2=Tackley|date=July 24, 2010|publisher=Cambridge University Press|doi=10.1017/CBO9780511780820|isbn=9780511780820}}</ref> and natural hazard<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/de/academic/subjects/earth-and-environmental-science/earth-science-general-interest/extreme-natural-hazards-disaster-risks-and-societal-implications|title=Extreme natural hazards disaster risks and societal implications|first1=Alik|last1=Ismail-Zadeh|date=April 14, 2014|website=Cambridge University Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Global risks: Pool knowledge to stem losses from disasters|first1=Susan L.|last1=Cutter|first2=Alik|last2=Ismail-Zadeh|first3=Irasema|last3=Alcántara-Ayala|first4=Orhan|last4=Altan|first5=Daniel N.|last5=Baker|first6=Salvano|last6=Briceño|first7=Harsh|last7=Gupta|first8=Ailsa|last8=Holloway|first9=David|last9=Johnston|first10=Gordon A.|last10=McBean|first11=Yujiro|last11=Ogawa|first12=Douglas|last12=Paton|first13=Emma|last13=Porio|first14=Rainer K.|last14=Silbereisen|first15=Kuniyoshi|last15=Takeuchi|first16=Giovanni B.|last16=Valsecchi|first17=Coleen|last17=Vogel|author17-link=Coleen Vogel|first18=Guoxiong|last18=Wu|date=June 18, ==Biography and academic career==
Born in Baku, Azerbaijan, Ismail-Zadeh attended the Bulbul specialized secondary music school of the [[Baku Academy of Music]] and Baku High School #134 (specialized in mathematics) between 1967 and 1978. He graduated from the [[Baku State University]] and the Lomonosov [[Moscow State University]] in 1983 before being awarded a Ph.D. degree in 1990 and D. Sc. ([[Habilitation]]) in 1997 from the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in Moscow, Russia. Ismail-Zadeh has been affiliated with the [[Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences]], Institute of Geology and Geophysics (1983-1986, 1990–1992).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gia.az/view.php?lang=en&menu=0|title=ANAS Institute of Geology and Geophysics Homepage|website=www.gia.az|access-date=23 April 2022|archive-date=17 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220517005443/https://www.gia.az/view.php?lang=en&menu=0|url-status=dead}}</ref> He has been chief scientist, research professor and scientific leader of research group "Computational Geodynamics and Geohazard Modeling" of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] Institute of Earthquake Prediction Theory and Mathematical Geophysics, Moscow (1992–2022).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mitp.ru|title=IEPT Homepage|website=www.mitp.ru}}</ref>

He has been a [[visiting scholar]], lecturer and professor at several universities and academic centers, including the [[University of Cambridge]] (UK),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.itg.cam.ac.uk/people.html|title=Institute of Theoretical Geophysics - Members and Friends|website=www.itg.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> [[University of California at Los Angeles]], the [[University of Tokyo]] (Japan),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eri.u-tokyo.ac.jp/kokusai/english/researchers/ismail-zadeh_a/ismail-zadeh_e.html|title=ERI International Office :: Visiting Researchers :: Ali Ismail-Zadeh|website=www.eri.u-tokyo.ac.jp}}</ref> [[Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris]] (France),<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Numerical modeling of crustal block-and-fault dynamics, earthquakes and slip rates in the Tibet-Himalayan region|first1=Alik|last1=Ismail-Zadeh|first2=Jean-Louis|last2=Le Mouël|first3=Alexander|last3=Soloviev|first4=Paul|last4=Tapponnier|first5=Inessa|last5=Vorovieva|date=June 30, 2007|journal=Earth and Planetary Science Letters|volume=258|issue=3|pages=465–485|doi=10.1016/j.epsl.2007.04.006|bibcode=2007E&PSL.258..465I}}</ref> the [[University of Uppsala]] (Sweden),<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Dynamic restoration of profiles across diapiric salt structures: numerical approach and its applications|first1=Alik T.|last1=Ismail-Zadeh|first2=Christopher J.|last2=Talbot|first3=Yuri A.|last3=Volozh|date=July 20, 2001|journal=Tectonophysics|volume=337|issue=1|pages=23–38|doi=10.1016/S0040-1951(01)00111-1|bibcode=2001Tectp.337...23I}}</ref> and the Abdus Salam [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in Trieste (Italy).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ictp.tv/diploma/search10-11.php?activityid=ESP&course=Geodynamics&order=olderfirst|title=EyA Recordings of the ICTP Diploma Programme|website=www.ictp.tv|access-date=21 October 2019|archive-date=30 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161230173209/http://www.ictp.tv/diploma/search10-11.php?activityid=ESP&course=Geodynamics&order=olderfirst|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Research==
Ismail-Zadeh has conducted research in the fields of [[geodynamics]], [[seismology]], [[sedimentary basin]]s and [[tectonics]] (incl. research for [[petroleum industry]]), [[geological hazard]]s, [[disaster risk reduction]] analysis, [[science diplomacy]], and [[history]]. He is a principal author and co-author of over 150 peer-reviewed papers and several books published by the [[Cambridge University Press]], [[Springer Nature]], and others.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://comgeodyn.org/lpub.html|title=A. Ismail-Zadeh List of Publications|website=comgeodyn.org}}</ref> Scientific results obtained by him and his group are as follows:

'''Inverse problems and data assimilation'''
* Introduction of data assimilation in models of geodynamics and applications to mantle (plume) dynamics.;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Schubert, G., Tsepelev, I., and Korotkii, A., Inverse problem of thermal convection: Numerical approach and application to mantle plume restoration, ''Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.'', '''145''', 99-114, 2004.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Schubert, G., Tsepelev, I., and Korotkii, A., Three-dimensional forward and backward numerical modeling of mantle plume evolution: Effects of thermal diffusion, ''J. Geophys. Res.'', '''111''', B06401, doi:10.1029/2005JB003782, 2006.</ref>
* Reconstruction of sinking [[lithosphere]] in the southeastern Carpathians;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Schubert, G., Tsepelev, I., and Korotkii, A., Thermal evolution and geometry of the descending lithosphere beneath the SE-Carpathians: An insight from the past, ''Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.'', '''273''', 68-79, 2008.</ref>
* Reconstruction of the western Pacific and Philippine plate subduction beneath the Japanese islands and implication on the Japan Sea opening;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Honda, S., and Tsepelev, I., Linking mantle upwelling with the lithosphere descent and the Japan Sea evolution: a hypothesis, ''Scientific Reports'', '''3''', 1137, doi: 10.1038/srep01137, 2013.</ref>
* Reconstruction of flow and temperature inside volcanic lava flow based on surface observations;<ref>Korotkii, A., Kovtunov, D., Ismail-Zadeh, A., Tsepelev, I., and Melnik, O., Quantitative reconstruction of thermal and dynamic characteristics of lava from surface thermal measurements, ''Geophys. J. Int.'', '''205''', 1767–1779, 2016.</ref>
* Restoration of sedimentary basin evolution complicated by salt tectonics: application to Pricaspian basin of the East European platform.<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Talbot, C.J., and Volozh, Yu.A., Dynamic restoration of profiles across diapiric salt structures: numerical approach and its applications, ''Tectonophysics'', '''337''', 21-36, 2001.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Tsepelev, I.A., Talbot, C.J., and Korotkii, A.I., Three-dimensional forward and backward modelling of diapirism: Numerical approach and its applicability to the evolution of salt structures in the Pricaspian basin, ''Tectonophysics'', '''387''', 81-103, 2004.</ref>

'''Lithosphere dynamics and seismicity'''
* Model of the block-and-fault dynamics<ref>Soloviev, A. A., and Ismail-Zadeh, A. T., Models of dynamics of block-and-fault systems, in ''Nonlinear Dynamics of the Lithosphere and Earthquake Prediction'', Keilis-Borok, V. I., and Soloviev, A. A. (eds.), pp. 69-138, Springer, Heidelberg, 2003.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Le Mouël, J.-L., and Soloviev, A., Modeling of extreme seismic events, in ''Extreme Events and Natural Hazards: The Complexity Perspective'', Sharma, S. A., Bunde, A., Dimri, V. P., and Baker, D. N. (eds.), Geophysical Monograph 196, American Geophysical Union, Washington, D. C., pp. 75-97, 2012.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Soloviev, A., Sokolov, V., Vorobieva, I., Muller, B., and Schilling, F., Quantitative modeling of the lithosphere dynamics, earthquakes and seismic hazard, ''Tectonophysics'', '''746''', 624-647, 2018.</ref>
* Quantitative models of a fault network interaction in the Tibet-Himalayan region to explain seismicity and slip rates at major regional faults;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Le Mouël, J.-L., Soloviev, A., Tapponnier, P., and Vorovieva, I., Numerical modeling of crustal block-and-fault dynamics, earthquakes and slip rates in the Tibet-Himalayan region, ''Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.'', '''258''', 465-485, 2007.</ref>
* Peculiarities of the Vrancea intermediate-depth seismicity<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Keilis-Borok, V.I., and Soloviev, A.A., Numerical modelling of earthquake flows in the southeastern Carpathians (Vrancea): Effect of a sinking slab, ''Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.'', '''111''', 267-274, 1999.</ref>

'''Seismic and volcanic hazard and risk'''
* Deterministic and probabilistic seismic hazard assessments for the Vrancea region (Romania), Tibet-Himalaya, and Shillong Plateau (India).<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Sokolov, V., and Bonier, K., Geodynamics, seismicity and seismic hazard of the south-eastern Carpathians, ''Natural Hazards'', '''42''', 493-514, 2007.</ref><ref>Sokolov, V., and Ismail-Zadeh, A., Seismic hazard from instrumentally recorded, historical and simulated earthquakes: Application to the Tibet-Himalayan region, ''Tectonophysics'', '''657''', 187-204, 2015.</ref><ref>Sokolov, V., and Ismail-Zadeh, A., On the use of multiple-site estimations in probabilistic seismic hazard assessment, ''Bull. Seismol. Soc. Am.'', '''106(5)''', 2233–2243, 2016.</ref><ref>Baro, O., Kumar, A., and Ismail-Zadeh, A., Seismic hazard assessment of the Shillong Plateau, India, ''Geomatics, Natural Hazards and Risk'', '''9(1)''', 841-861, 2018.</ref> Earthquake risk assessment for the Baku city (Azerbaijan);<ref>Babayev, G., Ismail-Zadeh, A., and Le Mouël, J.-L., Scenario-based earthquake hazard and risk assessment for Baku (Azerbaijan), ''Nat. Hazards Earth Sys. Sci.'', '''10''', 2697-2712, 2010.</ref>
* Volcanic lava hazard evaluation based on lava flow with debris.<ref>Tsepelev, I., Ismail-Zadeh, A., Melnik, O., and Korotkii, A., Numerical modelling of fluid flow with rafts: An application to lava flows, ''J. Geodyn.'', '''97''', 31-41, 2016.</ref>

'''Tectonic stress'''
* Understanding of tectonic stress localization and its change in the lithospheric slab in terms of style of the slab subduction;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Mueller, B., and Wenzel, F., Modelling of descending slab evolution beneath the SE-Carpathians: Implications for seismicity, in ''Perspectives in Modern Seismology'', Lecture Notes in Earth Sciences, Volume 105, pp. 205-226, F. Wenzel (Ed.), Springer-Verlag, Heidelberg, 2005</ref>
* Explanation of coexisting shortening - extension and seismic activity in the Central Apennines by the buoyancy of the lithosphere;<ref>Aoudia, A., Ismail-Zadeh, A., and Romanelli, F., Buoyancy-driven deformation and contemporary tectonic stress in the lithosphere beneath Central Italy, Terra Nova, 19(6), 490-495, 2007.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Aoudia, A., and Panza, G., Three-dimensional numerical modeling of contemporary mantle flow and tectonic stress beneath the Central Mediterranean, ''Tectonophysics'', '''482''', 226-236, 2010.</ref>
* Tectonic stress localization in the Vrancea earthquake-prone body beneath the south-eastern Carpathians.<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Panza, G.F., and Naimark, B.M., Stress in the descending relic slab beneath Vrancea, Romania, ''Pure Appl. Geophys.'', '''157''', 111-130, 2000.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Mueller, B., and Schubert, G., Three-dimensional modeling of present-day tectonic stress beneath the earthquake-prone southeastern Carpathians based on integrated analysis of seismic, heat flow, and gravity observations, ''Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.'', '''149''', 81-98, 2005.</ref>

'''Sedimentary basins'''
* Introduction of eclogitization-induced mantle flow mechanism for sedimentary basin evolution;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Naimark, B.M., and Lobkovsky, L.I., Hydrodynamic model of sedimentary basin formation based on development and subsequent phase transformation of a magmatic lens in the upper mantle, ''Comput. Seism. Geodyn.'', '''3''', 42-53, Amer. Geophys. Union, Washington D.C., 1996. DOI: 10.1029/CS003p0042.</ref>
* Quantitative models of the evolution of intracratonic sedimentary basins in North America (Illinois, Michigan and Williston basins),<ref>Naimark B.M., and Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Numerical models of subsidence mechanism in intracratonic basin: Application to North American basins, ''Geophys. J. Int.'', '''123''', 149-160, 1995.</ref> East European (Dnieper-Donets, Moscow, Pre-Ural, Timan-Pechora basins),<ref>Lobkovsky, L.I., Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Krasovsky, S.S., Kuprienko, P.Ya., and Cloetingh, S., Origin of gravity anomalies and possible forming mechanism of the Dnieper-Donets Basin, ''Tectonophysics'', '''268''', 281-292, 1996.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Kostyuchenko, S.L., and Naimark, B.M., The Timan-Pechora Basin (northeastern European Russia): tectonic subsidence analysis and a model of formation mechanism, ''Tectonophysics'', '''283''', 205-218, 1997.</ref> and Siberian ([[Tunguska Basin|Tunguska]] and Viluy basins) platforms;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Naimark, B.M., and Kostyuchenko, S.L., Quantitative modelling of the Tunguska Basin evolution in the Palaeozoic: A role of eclogitization within the uppermost mantle, ''J. Geodyn.'', '''23''', 47-63, 1997.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., The Devonian to Permian subsidence mechanisms in basins of the East-European platform, ''J. Geodyn.'', '''26''', 69-83, 1998.</ref>
* Models of geothermal evolution of the Astrakhan Arch of the Pricaspian Basin.<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Wilhelm, H., and Volozh, Yu, Geothermal evolution of the Astrakhan arch region of the Pricaspian Basin, ''Int. J. Earth Sci.'', '''97''', 1029-1043, 2008.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Wilhelm, H., Volozh, Y., and Tinakin, O., The Astrakhan Arch of the Pricaspian Basin: Geothermal analysis and modelling, ''Basin Research'', '''22''', 751–764, 2010.</ref>

'''Numerical methods for geodynamics'''
* New numerical methods and algorithms of an enhanced accuracy to study problems of Earth's dynamics;<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., and Tackley, P. J., ''Computational Methods for Geodynamics'', Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, 2010.</ref>
* Numerical methodology for data assimilation in geodynamics (backward advection, variational/adjoint, and quasi-reversibility methods).<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A., Korotkii, A., and Tsepelev, ''Data-driven Numerical Modeling in Geodynamics: Methods and Applications'', Springer, Heidelberg, 2016.</ref>

'''Gravitational and thermal instability'''
* Theoretical results in problems of Rayleigh-Taylor and Rayleigh-Bernard instabilities of the (geo) structures including analysis of Newtonian, Maxwell, non-Newtonian power law, and perfectly plastic rheologies;<ref>Naimark, B.M., and Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Gravitational instability of Maxwell upper mantle, ''Comput. Seism. Geodyn.'', '''1''', 36-42, Amer. Geophys. Union, Washington D.C., 1994. DOI: 10.1029/CS001p0036.</ref><ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Gravitational instability and propagation of tectonic waves in a two-layer model of the upper mantle, ''Comput. Seism. Geodyn.'', '''2''', 76-80, Amer. Geophys. Union, Washington D.C., 1994. DOI: 10.1029/CS002p0076.</ref><ref>Doglioni, C., Ismail-Zadeh, A., Panza, G., and Riguzzi, F., Lithosphere-asthenosphere viscosity contrast and decoupling, ''Phys. Earth Planet. Inter.'', '''189''', 1-8, 2011.</ref>
* Applications to salt diapirism: Models of salt structure evolution in the Pricaspain Basin<ref>Ismail-Zadeh, A.T., Huppert, H.E., and Lister, J.R., Gravitational and buckling instabilities of a rheologically layered structure: Implications for salt diapirism, ''Geophys. J. Int.'', '''148(2)''', 288-302, 2002.</ref>

==Organizational activities==

Alik Ismail-Zadeh is active in promoting science research, science excellency and science for society worldwide. From 2018 to 2021, Ismail-Zadeh served as (inaugural) secretary-general of the [[International Science Council]] (ISC).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://council.science/profile/alik-ismail-zadeh/|title=Alik Ismail-Zadeh|accessdate=26 May 2023}}</ref> Also, he was (inaugural) chair of the ISC Awards Programme Committee. Currently, he is Vice-Chair of the ISC Fellowship Council<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://council.science/about-us/fellows/|title=ISC Fellowship Council}}</ref> and Chair of the Scientific Committee of the Integrated Research on Disaster Risk Programme<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irdrinternational.org/irdr_community/scientific_committee/|title=IRDR Scientific Committee}}</ref> jointly co-sponsored by ISC and [[United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction]] (UNDRR).

Ismail-Zadeh was elected secretary-general of the [[International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics]] (IUGG) in 2007, and served the union for 12 years in this capacity (until 2019).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iugg.org/about/iugg-administration|title=Administration of the IUGG {{pipe}} Union Geodesique et Geophysique Internationale|website=www.iugg.org}}</ref> He also served the union as chair of the IUGG Commission on Geophysical Risk and Sustainability (2003–2007). He is chair of the IUGG Commission on Mathematical Geophysics (2019–2027).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iugg.org/associations-commissions/commissions/cmg|title=IUGG Commission on Mathematical Geophysics|website=www.iugg.org}}</ref> He has been a member of the scientific council of the UNESCO East African Institute for Fundamental Research (EAIFR), Kigali, Rwanda, since 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://eaifr.ictp.it/about/governance/|title=Governance {{pipe}} EAIFR|website=eaifr.ictp.it}}</ref>

He was a founding member and the (inaugural) governing board member of the European Association for the Promotion of Science and Technology ([[EuroScience]]);<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.euroscience.org/|title=EuroScience Governing Board|website=EuroScience|access-date=21 October 2019|archive-date=25 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925085145/https://www.euroscience.org/|url-status=dead}}</ref> (inaugural) president of the Natural Hazards Section of the [[American Geophysical Union]] (AGU);<ref>[https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/AGU/8ce4990c-6cf2-4c79-b08d-d3d63b5556fa/UploadedImages/Minutes_May25_09.pdf AGU Natural Hazards Focus Group]</ref> chair of the Committee on Sergei Soloviev Medal on Natural Hazards of the [[European Geosciences Union]] (EGU); chair of the steering committee of GeoUnions grouped under the [[International Science Council]];<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.icsu-geounions.org/membership.php|title=ICSU GeoUnions - Membership|website=www.icsu-geounions.org}}</ref> and council member of the [[UNESCO]] International Geoscience Program.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.unesco.org/international-geoscience-programme/|title=UNESCO IGCP |website=www.unesco.org|date=21 April 2022}}</ref> He served the [[Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization]] [CTBTO],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ctbto.org/news-and-events/science-and-technology-conference|title=CTBTO Science and Technology Conferences|website=www.ctbto.org}}</ref> the Group on Earth Observations [GEO],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://earthobservations.org/index.php | title=GEO }}</ref> the [[United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction]] [UNDRR]<ref>[https://www.preventionweb.net/files/58809_scienceandpolicyforumconceptnote.pdf Science and policy forum concept note] preventionweb.net</ref><ref>[https://www.agw.kit.edu/downloads/Petrophysik/GP2019_AIZ.pdf Petrophysik] agw.kit.edu</ref> and the United Nations [[International Year of Planet Earth]] [IYPE; 2007-2009]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.yearofplanetearth.org/|title=Planet Earth - Earth Sciences for Society|website=www.yearofplanetearth.org}}</ref> in various capacities.

Alik Ismail-Zadeh has been editor or member of several editorial/advisory boards, including ''[[Surveys in Geophysics]]'', Springer Nature;<ref>[https://www.springer.com/journal/10712/editors Surveys in Geophysics. Editors] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191021144510/https://www.springer.com/journal/10712/editors |date=2019-10-21 }}</ref> Special Publications of Geodesy and Geophysics series, Cambridge University Press;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/series/special-publications-of-the-international-union-of-geodesy-and-geophysics/C35865315590ECF1F6098B677D82AFA8|title=Special Publications of the International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics|website=Cambridge Core}}</ref> Computational Seismology and Geodynamics, American Geophysical Union<ref>{{Cite book |title=Selected Papers from Volumes 33 and 34 of Vychislitel'naya Seysmologiya |series=Computational Seismology and Geodynamics |editor-first1=Alik|editor-last1=Ismail-Zade|editor-first2=Edo|editor-last2=Nyland|editor-first3=Robert|editor-last3=Odom|editor-first4=Mrinal|editor-last4=Sen|editor-first5=V.
